items.q: Genetic (atypical) HUS is caused by activation of the alternate complement pathway, with the complement profile:
items.exp: A/w: low C3, normal C4. (Book p754)

items.q: Match each genetic type of atypical HUS with its prognostic label — 1) Complement factor-H mutation 2) Complement factor-B 3) Membrane cofactor-P (MCP) … A) Worst prognosis B) Best prognosis C) m/c mutation
items.exp: Factor-H (m/c) mutation; factor-B worst prognosis; MCP best prognosis; factor-I also listed. (Book p754)

items.q: Among sporadic drug-induced HUS agents, the pair also bracketed to TTP is:
items.exp: Ticlopidine + clopidogrel are annotated "TTP also" among drug-induced causes. (Book p754)

items.q: The immune-mediated HUS list contains quinine, gemcitabine, quetiapine and cotrimoxazole; the odd one out from that list is:
items.exp: Mitomycin sits under sporadic drug-induced causes, not immune-mediated HUS. (Book p754)

items.q: On the peripheral blood smear, schistocytes become significant beyond:
items.exp: Peripheral blood smear: schistocyte (>2% significant). (Book p754)

items.q: The hemolysis work-up in HUS shows:
opts: ↑ LDH, negative Coombs, ↑ indirect bilirubin, ↓ haptoglobin with normal PT/APTT
↑ LDH, positive Coombs, ↓ indirect bilirubin, ↑ haptoglobin
Normal LDH, negative Coombs, ↑ direct bilirubin, ↓ haptoglobin
items.exp: Blood investigation: ↑ LDH, −ve Coombs test, ↑ indirect bilirubin, ↓ haptoglobin level, normal PT/APTT. (Book p754)

items.q: Match each column with its complement signature — 1) Atypical HUS pathway 2) SLE pathway 3) Atypical HUS C4 … A) Classical B) Alternative C) Normal
items.exp: Atypical HUS: alternative pathway, low C3 (N) C4; SLE: classical pathway, low C3 low C4. (Book p754)
